missing_security_headers.title: Missing HTTP Security Response Headers
missing_security_headers.summary: Add standard browser defense-in-depth HTTP headers (Content-Security-Policy, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy) globally via response middleware or reverse proxy configuration.
missing_security_headers.root_cause_template: The response from {method} {path} ({parameter}) omits one or more recommended HTTP security headers. Without these browser-enforced guardrails, the application is more exposed to clickjacking, MIME-type sniffing, referrer leakage, and script injection.

snippets.after:
from fastapi import FastAPI, Request

app = FastAPI()

@app.middleware("http")
async def add_security_headers(request: Request, call_next):
    response = await call_next(request)
    response.headers["X-Content-Type-Options"] = "nosniff"
    response.headers["X-Frame-Options"] = "DENY"
    response.headers["Referrer-Policy"] = "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"
    response.headers["Permissions-Policy"] = "geolocation=(), microphone=(), camera=()"
    response.headers["Content-Security-Policy"] = "default-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; object-src 'none'"
    return response

from flask import Flask

app = Flask(__name__)

@app.after_request
def set_security_headers(response):
    response.headers["X-Content-Type-Options"] = "nosniff"
    response.headers["X-Frame-Options"] = "DENY"
    response.headers["Referrer-Policy"] = "strict-origin-when-cross-origin"
    response.headers["Permissions-Policy"] = "geolocation=(), microphone=(), camera=()"
    response.headers["Content-Security-Policy"] = "default-src 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'; object-src 'none'"
    return response

weak_csp.title: Weak or Permissive Content-Security-Policy (CSP)
weak_csp.summary: Tighten the Content-Security-Policy header by removing 'unsafe-inline', 'unsafe-eval', and wildcard '*' sources from script-src/default-src, and explicitly restricting default-src, object-src, and base-uri.
weak_csp.root_cause_template: The Content-Security-Policy returned on {method} {path} ({parameter}) uses overly permissive directives (such as 'unsafe-inline', 'unsafe-eval', '*', or missing default-src/object-src), weakening its ability to block Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) payloads.

snippets.before: response.headers["Content-Security-Policy"] = "default-src * 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval'"
snippets.after:
import secrets

nonce = secrets.token_urlsafe(16)
response.headers["Content-Security-Policy"] = (
    f"default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-{nonce}'; "
    "style-src 'self'; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'"
)

snippets.before:
<?php
header("Content-Security-Policy: default-src * 'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval'");
snippets.after:
<?php
$nonce = base64_encode(random_bytes(16));
header(
    "Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'nonce-{$nonce}'; " .
    "object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'"
);

snippets.before:
<button onclick="submitOrder()">Order</button>
<script>console.log('inline without nonce');</script>
snippets.after:
<!-- Move inline handlers to external scripts or attach a per-request CSP nonce -->
<button id="order-btn" type="button">Order</button>
<script src="/static/js/order.js" defer></script>

server_banner_leak.title: Server Technology and Version Banner Disclosure
server_banner_leak.summary: Suppress or strip version-disclosing Server and X-Powered-By HTTP response headers so attackers cannot trivially fingerprint exact framework or runtime versions.
server_banner_leak.root_cause_template: The HTTP response for {method} {path} ({parameter}) exposes exact server or framework version details in response headers, aiding automated reconnaissance for version-specific CVEs.

snippets.before:
# Uvicorn sends 'Server: uvicorn' by default
uvicorn.run("app:app", host="127.0.0.1", port=8000)
snippets.after:
# Disable the Server header in Uvicorn and strip X-Powered-By in middleware
@app.middleware("http")
async def strip_banners(request: Request, call_next):
    response = await call_next(request)
    if "x-powered-by" in response.headers:
        del response.headers["x-powered-by"]
    return response

# Run with: uvicorn app:app --no-server-header

snippets.before:
# Werkzeug/Flask exposes 'Server: Werkzeug/3.x Python/3.x'
app.run(host="127.0.0.1", port=5000)

; php.ini
expose_php = On
<meta name="generator" content="WordPress 5.8.1">
snippets.after:
<!-- Remove CMS/framework version generator meta tags from HTML templates -->
<meta charset="utf-8">

verbose_error_pages.title: Verbose Error Pages and Stack Trace Disclosure
verbose_error_pages.summary: Disable debug error pages in deployed environments and register a global exception handler that logs detailed stack traces server-side while returning a generic error message to clients.
verbose_error_pages.root_cause_template: The endpoint {method} {path} ({parameter}) returned raw internal exception details or framework stack traces in the HTTP body, leaking source file paths, library versions, or query structures.

snippets.after:
import logging
from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from fastapi.responses import JSONResponse

logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
app = FastAPI(debug=False)

@app.exception_handler(Exception)
async def unhandled_exception_handler(request: Request, exc: Exception):
    logger.exception("Unhandled error on %s", request.url.path)
    return JSONResponse(status_code=500, content={"error": "Internal server error"})

snippets.before:
app = Flask(__name__)
app.run(debug=True)
snippets.after:
import logging
from flask import Flask, jsonify

app = Flask(__name__)
app.config["DEBUG"] = False
app.config["PROPAGATE_EXCEPTIONS"] = False

@app.errorhandler(500)
def handle_internal_error(err):
    app.logger.exception("Internal server error: %s", err)
    return jsonify({"error": "An unexpected error occurred."}), 500

snippets.before:
<?php
ini_set("display_errors", "1");
error_reporting(E_ALL);
snippets.after:
<?php
ini_set("display_errors", "0");
ini_set("log_errors", "1");
set_exception_handler(function (Throwable $e): void {
    error_log($e->getMessage() . "\n" . $e->getTraceAsString());
    http_response_code(500);
    echo "An unexpected error occurred.";
});

insecure_cookies.title: Session Cookie Missing Security Attributes
insecure_cookies.summary: Set HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax (or Strict), and Secure (over HTTPS) flags on all authentication and session cookies so scripts and cross-site requests cannot steal or misuse session identifiers.
insecure_cookies.root_cause_template: A session-related cookie issued by {method} {path} ({parameter}) lacks one or more protective flags (HttpOnly, SameSite, or Secure), increasing the risk of session hijacking via XSS, network sniffing, or CSRF.

snippets.before: response.set_cookie(key="session_id", value=token)
snippets.after:
response.set_cookie(
    key="session_id",
    value=token,
    httponly=True,
    secure=True,
    samesite="lax",
    path="/",
)

snippets.before:
app = Flask(__name__)
# Defaults allow JS access or missing SameSite in older configs
snippets.after:
app = Flask(__name__)
app.config.update(
    SESSION_COOKIE_HTTPONLY=True,
    SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE=True,
    SESSION_COOKIE_SAMESITE="Lax",
)

snippets.before: res.cookie("session_id", token);

<?php
setcookie("PHPSESSID", $token);
snippets.after:
<?php
session_set_cookie_params([
    "httponly" => true,
    "secure" => true,
    "samesite" => "Lax",
    "path" => "/",
]);
session_start();

snippets.before:
<script>
  // Never store session tokens in document.cookie from client JS
  document.cookie = "session_id=" + token;
</script>
snippets.after:
<!-- Issue session cookies exclusively from the backend with HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Lax -->
<meta http-equiv="X-UA-Compatible" content="IE=edge">

insecure_transport.title: Insecure Transport (Cleartext Credentials or Missing HSTS)
insecure_transport.summary: Enforce HTTPS with a 301 redirect from HTTP and emit a Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS) header so credentials and session tokens are never transmitted in cleartext.
insecure_transport.root_cause_template: The endpoint {method} {path} ({parameter}) either submits sensitive password inputs over unencrypted HTTP or serves HTTPS traffic without a Strict-Transport-Security header, leaving users vulnerable to eavesdropping or SSL stripping.

snippets.before:
app = FastAPI()
# Served over plain HTTP without HSTS or redirect
snippets.after:
from fastapi import FastAPI, Request
from starlette.middleware.httpsredirect import HTTPSRedirectMiddleware

app = FastAPI()
app.add_middleware(HTTPSRedirectMiddleware)

@app.middleware("http")
async def add_hsts(request: Request, call_next):
    response = await call_next(request)
    if request.url.scheme == "https":
        response.headers["Strict-Transport-Security"] = "max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains"
    return response

snippets.before: app.post("/login", loginHandler);

<?php
// Accepts plain HTTP login submissions
process_login($_POST);
snippets.after:
<?php
if (empty($_SERVER["HTTPS"]) || $_SERVER["HTTPS"] === "off") {
    header("Location: https://" . $_SERVER["HTTP_HOST"] . $_SERVER["REQUEST_URI"], true, 301);
    exit;
}
header("Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains");
process_login($_POST);

snippets.before:
<form action="http://app.local/login" method="POST">
  <input type="password" name="password">
</form>
snippets.after:
<!-- Use relative or explicit HTTPS form actions and upgrade insecure requests -->
<form action="/login" method="POST" autocomplete="on">
  <input type="password" name="password" autocomplete="current-password" required>
</form>

csrf_missing_token.title: State-Changing Form Missing Anti-CSRF Token
csrf_missing_token.summary: Generate a cryptographically random per-session or per-request anti-CSRF token, embed it as a hidden field in every state-changing HTML form, and validate it in constant time on the server.
csrf_missing_token.root_cause_template: The state-changing HTML form submitted to {method} {path} ({parameter}) does not include an anti-CSRF token field. A malicious website could trick an authenticated user's browser into submitting forged requests on their behalf.

snippets.after:
import hmac
from fastapi import Form, HTTPException, Request

@app.post("/profile/update")
async def update_profile(
    request: Request,
    email: str = Form(...),
    csrf_token: str = Form(...),
):
    expected = request.cookies.get("csrf_token", "")
    if not expected or not hmac.compare_digest(csrf_token, expected):
        raise HTTPException(status_code=403, detail="Invalid CSRF token")
    save_email(email)

from flask import Flask, request
from flask_wtf.csrf import CSRFProtect

app = Flask(__name__)
app.config["SECRET_KEY"] = "replace-with-env-secret"
csrf = CSRFProtect(app)

@app.post("/profile/update")
def update_profile():
    save_email(request.form["email"])

snippets.before:
<?php
// Directly processes POST without CSRF check
update_email($_POST["email"]);
snippets.after:
<?php
session_start();
if (empty($_POST["csrf_token"]) || !hash_equals($_SESSION["csrf_token"] ?? "", $_POST["csrf_token"])) {
    http_response_code(403);
    exit("Invalid CSRF token");
}
update_email($_POST["email"]);

snippets.before:
<form action="/profile/update" method="POST">
  <input type="email" name="email">
  <button type="submit">Save</button>
</form>
snippets.after:
<form action="/profile/update" method="POST">
  <input type="hidden" name="csrf_token" value="{{ csrf_token }}">
  <input type="email" name="email" required>
  <button type="submit">Save</button>
</form>

outdated_js_components.title: Outdated Client-Side JavaScript Library with Known Vulnerabilities
outdated_js_components.summary: Upgrade the affected client-side JavaScript library to a patched release, pin versions via a lockfile, and add Subresource Integrity (SRI) hashes for externally hosted bundles.
outdated_js_components.root_cause_template: The page or asset loaded from {method} {path} ({parameter}) references an outdated JavaScript library version with publicly disclosed CVEs (such as DOM XSS or prototype pollution).

snippets.before:
# Serving an outdated vendored library from static/
# static/js/jquery-1.12.4.min.js
snippets.after:
# Replace vendored static/js/jquery-1.12.4.min.js with jquery-3.7.1.min.js
# and mount static assets with explicit versioned filenames
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles

app.mount("/static", StaticFiles(directory="static"), name="static")

snippets.before:
<!-- templates/base.html -->
<script src="{{ url_for('static', filename='js/jquery-2.1.4.min.js') }}"></script>
snippets.after:
<!-- templates/base.html — upgrade to a patched version -->
<script src="{{ url_for('static', filename='js/jquery-3.7.1.min.js') }}" defer></script>

snippets.before:
<?php
echo '<script src="/assets/js/bootstrap-3.3.7.min.js"></script>';
snippets.after:
<?php
// Serve upgraded, patched frontend assets
echo '<script src="/assets/js/bootstrap-5.3.3.bundle.min.js" defer></script>';

snippets.before: <script src="/static/jquery-3.4.1.min.js"></script>
snippets.after: <script src="/static/jquery-3.7.1.min.js" crossorigin="anonymous" defer></script>

cors_misconfig.title: Permissive Cross-Origin Resource Sharing (CORS) Policy
cors_misconfig.summary: Replace arbitrary Origin reflection, 'null' origins, and credentialed wildcards with an explicit allowlist of exact trusted origins.
cors_misconfig.root_cause_template: The endpoint {method} {path} ({parameter}) echoes untrusted Origin headers or combines permissive Access-Control-Allow-Origin rules with credentials, enabling malicious sites to read authenticated API responses cross-origin.

snippets.before:
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware

app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=["*"],
    allow_credentials=True,
    allow_methods=["*"],
    allow_headers=["*"],
)
snippets.after:
from fastapi.middleware.cors import CORSMiddleware

ALLOWED_ORIGINS = ["http://localhost:3000", "http://127.0.0.1:3000"]
app.add_middleware(
    CORSMiddleware,
    allow_origins=ALLOWED_ORIGINS,
    allow_credentials=True,
    allow_methods=["GET", "POST", "PATCH", "DELETE"],
    allow_headers=["Authorization", "Content-Type"],
)

snippets.before:
const cors = require("cors");
app.use(cors({ origin: true, credentials: true }));

<?php
header("Access-Control-Allow-Origin: " . ($_SERVER["HTTP_ORIGIN"] ?? "*"));
header("Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true");
snippets.after:
<?php
$allowedOrigins = ["http://localhost:3000", "http://127.0.0.1:3000"];
$origin = $_SERVER["HTTP_ORIGIN"] ?? "";
if (in_array($origin, $allowedOrigins, true)) {
    header("Access-Control-Allow-Origin: " . $origin);
    header("Access-Control-Allow-Credentials: true");
    header("Vary: Origin");
}

snippets.before:
<script>
fetch("http://localhost:8000/api/me", { credentials: "include" });
</script>
snippets.after:
<!-- Prefer same-origin API routes or configure an exact Origin allowlist on the backend -->
<script>
fetch("/api/me", { credentials: "same-origin" });
</script>

sqli_error_based.title: Error-Based SQL Injection
sqli_error_based.summary: Replace string-concatenated SQL with parameterized queries (bound placeholders) or ORM query builders so untrusted input is always treated strictly as data, never as executable SQL syntax.
sqli_error_based.root_cause_template: Untrusted user input sent via {method} {path} (parameter: {parameter}) is concatenated directly into a SQL statement, causing database syntax errors when quote characters are supplied and exposing the database to arbitrary query manipulation.

snippets.before:
from sqlalchemy import text

query = text(f"SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = '{user}'")
row = db.execute(query).fetchone()
snippets.after:
from sqlalchemy import select

stmt = select(User).where(User.username == user)
row = db.execute(stmt).scalar_one_or_none()

cursor.execute(
    "SELECT id, username FROM users WHERE username = ?",
    (request.form["user"],),
)

snippets.before:
const sql = `SELECT id, username FROM users WHERE username = '${req.body.user}'`;
const result = await db.query(sql);
snippets.after:
const sql = "SELECT id, username FROM users WHERE username = $1";
const result = await db.query(sql, [req.body.user]);

snippets.before:
<?php
$stmt = $pdo->query("SELECT id, username FROM users WHERE username = '" . $_POST['user'] . "'");
snippets.after:
<?php
$stmt = $pdo->prepare("SELECT id, username FROM users WHERE username = :user");
$stmt->execute(["user" => $_POST["user"]]);

snippets.before: <input type="text" name="user">
snippets.after:
<!-- Always use parameterized SQL on the server; add HTML constraints only as UX defense-in-depth -->
<input type="text" name="user" maxlength="64" pattern="[A-Za-z0-9_.@-]+" required>

sqli_boolean_diff.title: Boolean-Based Blind SQL Injection
sqli_boolean_diff.summary: Use parameterized prepared statements or ORM bindings for every query predicate and strictly validate expected input types (such as integers or allowlisted column names).
sqli_boolean_diff.root_cause_template: The application changes its response behavior on {method} {path} (parameter: {parameter}) when true versus false SQL boolean expressions are injected, indicating that raw user input is evaluated inside a SQL WHERE clause.

snippets.before:
query = text(f"SELECT * FROM products WHERE id = {item_id}")
item = db.execute(query).fetchone()
snippets.after:
from sqlalchemy import text

query = text("SELECT * FROM products WHERE id = :item_id")
item = db.execute(query, {"item_id": int(item_id)}).fetchone()

snippets.before:
item_id = request.args.get("id", "")
cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM products WHERE id = " + item_id)
snippets.after:
item_id = request.args.get("id", type=int)
if item_id is None:
    abort(400)
cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM products WHERE id = ?", (item_id,))

snippets.before:
const sql = "SELECT * FROM products WHERE id = " + req.query.id;
const rows = await db.query(sql);

<?php
$res = $pdo->query("SELECT * FROM products WHERE id = " . $_GET["id"]);
snippets.after:
<?php
$id = filter_input(INPUT_GET, "id", FILTER_VALIDATE_INT);
if ($id === false || $id === null) { http_response_code(400); exit; }
$stmt = $pdo->prepare("SELECT * FROM products WHERE id = :id");
$stmt->execute(["id" => $id]);

snippets.before: <input type="text" name="id">
snippets.after:
<!-- Enforce prepared statements server-side; restrict numeric inputs in HTML for UX -->
<input type="number" name="id" min="1" step="1" required>

xss_reflected.title: Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
xss_reflected.summary: Apply context-aware output encoding (auto-escaping templates, HTML entity encoding, and safe DOM APIs like textContent) whenever rendering untrusted input, reinforced with a strict Content-Security-Policy.
xss_reflected.root_cause_template: User-supplied input on {method} {path} (parameter: {parameter}) is echoed back into an HTML response without proper output escaping, allowing attacker-controlled markup or scripts to execute in a victim's browser.

snippets.after: Results for " . $safeQuery . "";

open_redirect.title: Unvalidated Open Redirect
open_redirect.summary: Restrict redirect destinations to relative local paths (single leading '/' without scheme/host) or an explicit server-side allowlist of destination identifiers.
open_redirect.root_cause_template: The endpoint {method} {path} (parameter: {parameter}) forwards users to an unvalidated external URL supplied in the request, enabling phishing campaigns that abuse your application's trusted origin.

snippets.before:
<?php
header("Location: " . ($_GET["next"] ?? "/"));
exit;
snippets.after:
<?php
$allowedPaths = ["/", "/dashboard", "/profile"];
$next = $_GET["next"] ?? "/";
$target = in_array($next, $allowedPaths, true) ? $next : "/";
header("Location: " . $target);
exit;

sensitive_files.title: Exposed Sensitive Configuration, Source, or Backup File
sensitive_files.summary: Remove backup, environment, and diagnostic artifacts from the web root, block dotfile paths (/.env, /.git) at the web server, and immediately rotate any exposed credentials.
sensitive_files.root_cause_template: The sensitive artifact at {method} {path} ({parameter}) is directly downloadable over HTTP, potentially leaking environment secrets, database schemas, source history, or API internals.

snippets.before:
# Mounting the entire project root exposes .env and .git!
app.mount("/", StaticFiles(directory="."), name="root")
snippets.after:
# Mount ONLY a dedicated public static directory and disable OpenAPI docs in production if internal
app = FastAPI(docs_url=None, redoc_url=None, openapi_url=None)
app.mount("/static", StaticFiles(directory="public/static"), name="static")

snippets.before:
# Serving files from the repository root exposes config files
app = Flask(__name__, static_folder=".")
snippets.after:
# Keep .env, backups, and source outside static_folder
app = Flask(__name__, static_folder="static", static_url_path="/static")

app.use(express.static(__dirname, { dotfiles: "allow" }));

# DocumentRoot set to project root containing .env and .git/
DocumentRoot /var/www/app

# Point DocumentRoot to public/ and deny hidden/backup files in .htaccess
# <FilesMatch "^(\.env|\.git|.*\.(bak|sql|log))$">
#   Require all denied
# </FilesMatch>
<?php
// Store .env outside public/ and load via __DIR__ . '/../.env'

snippets.after: Public API Guide

directory_listing.title: Web Server Directory Listing Enabled
directory_listing.summary: Disable automatic directory indexing in the web server or static file handler so visitors cannot enumerate internal assets, uploads, or backup files.
directory_listing.root_cause_template: Requesting {method} {path} ({parameter}) returned an auto-generated directory index listing files on the server, exposing internal filenames and unlinked resources.

snippets.after:
from fastapi.staticfiles import StaticFiles

# Starlette StaticFiles disables directory listing by default (returns 404)
app.mount("/uploads", StaticFiles(directory="uploads", html=False), name="uploads")

const serveIndex = require("serve-index");
app.use("/uploads", express.static("uploads"), serveIndex("uploads"));

forced_browsing_admin.title: Unauthenticated Access to Administrative or Privileged Endpoint
forced_browsing_admin.summary: Enforce server-side authentication and role-based authorization (RBAC) middleware on every administrative route, returning 401/403 by default when a valid admin session is absent.
forced_browsing_admin.root_cause_template: The administrative route {method} {path} ({parameter}) returned privileged content directly without requiring authentication or administrator role verification, allowing unauthorized forced browsing.

snippets.before:
<?php
// admin.php renders directly without role check
include "admin_dashboard.php";
snippets.after:
<?php
session_start();
if (empty($_SESSION["user_id"]) || ($_SESSION["role"] ?? "") !== "admin") {
    http_response_code(403);
    exit("Forbidden");
}
include "admin_dashboard.php";

snippets.before: Admin
snippets.after: {% if current_user and current_user.role == 'admin' %} Admin Console {% endif %}

idor_heuristic.title: Potential Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR — Manual Verification Needed)
idor_heuristic.summary: Verify object ownership on the server for every request by scoping database queries to the authenticated user's ID (e.g., WHERE id = :id AND owner_id = :current_user_id) and prefer unguessable UUIDs.
idor_heuristic.root_cause_template: Probing an adjacent numeric identifier on {method} {path} (parameter: {parameter}) returned another distinct HTTP 200 record. Because this heuristic cannot tell whether records are intentionally public, manually confirm that object-level ownership checks are enforced.

snippets.before:
<?php
$stmt = $pdo->prepare("SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = :id");
$stmt->execute(["id" => $_GET["id"]]);
snippets.after:
<?php
session_start();
$stmt = $pdo->prepare("SELECT * FROM orders WHERE id = :id AND owner_id = :owner_id");
$stmt->execute([
    "id" => (int) $_GET["id"],
    "owner_id" => (int) $_SESSION["user_id"],
]);
$order = $stmt->fetch();
if (!$order) { http_response_code(404); exit; }

snippets.before:
<!-- Relying on hidden user_id form fields can be tampered with by clients -->
<input type="hidden" name="user_id" value="42">
snippets.after:
<!-- Never trust client-supplied user_id; derive the owner from the authenticated session on the server -->
<form action="/api/orders" method="POST">
  <input type="text" name="item_sku" required>
</form>
